title: Nadia's Napkin Nightmare
markdown:
Nadia the hedgehog, apron neat, felt her quills prickle. Inspection Day at the Grand Station Buffet meant Inspector Grumbles, whose sharp eyes always found her book stall a bit too delightfully messy. She had spent a week colour-coding and alphabetising, exhausted, hoping to be seen as competent, not merely a creature who loved old books. Last year he had called her stall “intriguing, albeit risking spontaneous combustion.” She feared she was a charming mess, decorative, not professional.

The loudspeaker crackled: one hour until inspection. Deviations from pristine presentation might close the stall. Not a lecture: the possible silencing of her beloved books.

She scurried to the station master’s office. Rafi the otter, calm, polishing spectacles, unofficial advisor. “I need your genius. Grumbles is coming. I have tried everything.”

He chuckled. “A rogue novel escaping its binding?”

She explained. The station whirled: clattering trays, hissing steam, Grumbles’ shadow.

“Ingenious is my middle name,” Rafi declared, then confessed it was Bartholomew. “What common buffet woe needs a dash of cleverness?”

“Napkins. Always jumbled. Messy.”

They retreated to an alcove that smelled of forgotten journeys. Rafi rummaged springs and sprockets. The first napkin launcher was too eager, thwacking passengers softly. Another made a bird’s-nest heap. Despair; quills on end. She almost pictured escaping to the quiet shop, old paper, safety.

Then he held up a smooth polished wooden tube. “The Auto-Sort Napkin Extruder. Feed them in the top; they emerge sorted. Mostly.”

They tested it. Blue, then white, then striped, tumbling neat. A soft satisfying whir. Hope. “Magnificent.” The Extruder sat proud on her counter.

Grumbles arrived, frown set, missing nothing. Nadia stood tall, heart a trapped hummingbird. Rafi nodded. She activated the dispenser.

Blue. White. As a lavender napkin was about to appear, a soft thwump from the rafters. A single impossibly soft white feather drifted down on a draft and landed precisely on the opening.

The machine choked, high-pitched. Lavender jammed. A sickening snap; crumpled napkins spewed onto the floor. A jarring clang. Her stomach plummeted. The beautiful device was a monument to failure.

Grumbles narrowed at the chaos. She braced. Rafi stepped forward with a small perfectly folded paper crane. “A token of our appreciation.”

Grumbles looked at her crestfallen face, hunched shoulders. “Avian interference.” A hint of amusement. “I recall my first inspection. Pastry dispenser, a bold sparrow. Quite the flap.”

She found her voice. “I just wanted to be impressive. I worry I am not taken seriously.”

Sternness softened. He picked up a crumpled napkin. “The most impressive thing is not a perfect machine, but a genuine effort to do better. Sometimes the best ideas come when we try to be helpful, not clever.” He confessed his own early impressive solutions had been similarly messy.

The inspection ended with surprisingly few admonishments. Later she watched another feather drift from the rafters. Instead of flinching, she smiled. The fear had not vanished; it no longer crushed. Earnestness outranked engineered perfection. Even Grumbles, it seemed, could appreciate that story. The pigeon nest in the rafters remained undisturbed, and the Extruder, silent, still sat on the counter like a lesson she did not need to run again.
characters: Nadia (hedgehog bookshop clerk), Rafi (otter mentor), Inspector Grumbles (buffet inspector)
